s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic skin condition with multiple whitish papules and pruritic lesions on the trunk
salient_findings: Numerous whitish papules on the back of more than 10 years' duration
Papules became pruritic and extended to the waist and anterior trunk
Folliculocentric papules with central keratin plugs and surrounding erythema
key_facts: Woman in her 60s presented with skin lesions
Lesions previously resolved with topical corticosteroids but flared after treatment discontinuation
No family history of similar lesions
Multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules on the back, waist, and inframammary area
Most lesions were folliculocentric under close inspection
Dermoscopy revealed central keratin plugs and structureless, whitish, and homogenous areas
Antinuclear antibody and hyperglobulinemia tests were negative
Biopsy specimen from back showed central follicular plug and epidermal atrophy
Papillary dermis was markedly thickened with homogenized collagens and sparse bandlike lymphocytic infiltration

shortlist.why_kept: Folliculocentric papules and central keratin plugs on dermoscopy

shortlist.label: Lichen Spinulosus
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules and folliculocentric lesions

shortlist.label: Keratosis Follicularis
shortlist.why_kept: Central follicular plug and epidermal atrophy on histopathology

shortlist.label: Grover Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic lesions and transient response to topical corticosteroids

shortlist.label: Phrynoderma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypopigmented, flat-topped papules and folliculocentric distribution

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules that are folliculocentric, along with dermoscopic findings of central keratin plugs and histopathologic evidence of central follicular plugs and epidermal atrophy, supports the diagnosis of Lichen Spinulosus.

rejected.label: Keratosis Pilaris
rejected.why: While keratosis pilaris also presents with folliculocentric lesions, the presence of flat-topped papules and the specific dermoscopic and histopathologic findings in this case are more characteristic of Lichen Spinulosus.

rejected.label: Keratosis Follicularis
rejected.why: This condition is less likely given the specific combination of clinical, dermoscopic, and histopathologic findings presented in the case.

rejected.label: Grover Disease
rejected.why: Grover Disease typically presents with sudden onset of multiple, discrete, skin-colored to reddish-brown papules, which does not match the long-standing, folliculocentric lesions described in this case.

rejected.label: Phrynoderma
rejected.why: Phrynoderma is characterized by follicular hyperkeratosis with a rough, sandpapery texture, usually associated with nutritional deficiencies, which is not indicated in this vignette.
